name: fabfilter-proq4-drum-deharsh
description: Surgical + SPECTRAL-DYNAMICS drum-bus clean-up on FabFilter Pro-Q 4, headless. HPF rumble, a static low-mid box cut, and a band_3 in SPECTRAL DYNAMICS mode at ~5 kHz that ducks ONLY the offending frequencies inside the band when they ring (Pro-Q 4's marquee feature — its built-in Soothe, beyond a whole-band dynamic EQ). Natural Phase globally (keeps drum transients); the spectral band runs linear-phase on itself. Validated on the Watercolors drum loop. Reproducible because it (a) FLATTENS first (disables all 24 bands — a bare Pedalboard load of Pro-Q restores FabFilter's last-saved curve, never assume flat) and (b) sets EVERY param on each used band explicitly, including band_3_dynamic_range and the spectral params (an unset dynamic_range inherits the restored state's value — the repro footgun this preset exists to avoid).
intended_for: a drum bus / drum loop that needs rumble removed, low-mid box tamed, and harsh ~4-6 kHz controlled only on the frequencies that spike (spectral), without dulling the steady top
plugin_build: FabFilter 'Pro-Q 4.vst3' (renders headless via Pedalboard 0.9.23, no-iLok; all 581 params are Pedalboard valid_values lists settable via setattr — numeric snap to grid, string enums exact)
notes: FLATTEN FIRST: a plain load_plugin restores FabFilter's last-saved state (the GUI curve), NOT a flat EQ — so disable all unused bands explicitly or the leftover curve rides your move. apply-vst-chain's float-only `parameters` dict CANNOT do this (it can't set band_N_used / band_N_shape / band_N_slope / band_N_spectral_enabled string enums, nor enable an Unused band) — use this harness (setattr) or a dumped state_path.

SET EVERY DYNAMIC PARAM EXPLICITLY: band_3 sets gain 0, dynamic_range -8, dynamics_enabled, threshold Auto, spectral_enabled, spectral_density 70. An UNSET band_3_dynamic_range silently inherits the restored state's value (we hit -4.11 from the screenshot session once) — so a 'dynamic' band with no explicit dynamic_range is NOT reproducible. gain is the static base (0 = flat); dynamic_range is the spectral excursion (-8 = ducks up to 8 dB on the offending freqs only).

band_3 is SPECTRAL DYNAMICS (Pro-Q 4's marquee feature): it ducks only the individual frequencies inside the ~5 kHz band that exceed the threshold, leaving the rest of the band (and steady cymbals) intact — the surgical step beyond a whole-band dynamic EQ. Push dynamic_range more negative and/or spectral_density higher for a stronger/narrower duck. For a plain whole-band dynamic de-harsh instead, set spectral_enabled false (it'll move more of the band).

Spectral forces band_3 to LINEAR PHASE on itself (adds latency by resolution) even though the global mode is Natural Phase; the other bands stay Natural Phase. Fine for de-harsh above ~1 kHz at Low/Medium resolution.

Numeric params snap to Pro-Q's valid-values grid (gain ~0.06 dB, freq log grid) — read back to confirm. Verify with measure-spectrum: expect <40 Hz gone, ~250 Hz down ~3 dB, and 4-6 kHz pulled down only on its peaks (a gentler, surgical move than a static cut of the same dB).
